interfaces.name: text
interfaces.constraints: String input and nonempty list drawn from html, url, unicode, lower and spell. Operations execute in that fixed order, irrespective of list order; duplicates do not repeat work. Unicode uses NFKC and lower uses lower(), not casefold(). Nonprintable non-whitespace characters are removed; whitespace is collapsed and stripped. Spell requires a nonempty string-key vocabulary of nonnegative integer counts, excluding booleans. ASCII alphabetic tokens use known original, then one-edit, then two-edit candidates; ties prefer higher count, shorter word, then lexicographically greatest candidate. Unknown tokens become lowercase. Vocabulary is not learned or modified. HTML/URL handling is regex cleanup, not a security sanitizer. Two-edit candidate generation may be expensive; caller bounds input size.

intake_interfaces.name: term_frequencies
intake_interfaces.constraints:
Score aligned distinct query terms against one document using BM25.

Uses log1p((N-df+.5)/(df+.5)) IDF and tf*(k1+1)/(tf+k1*(1-b+b*dl/avgdl)).
Query terms have unit weight. Counts are Python integers in [0,2**53];
corpus size is positive, df <= N, and sum(tf) <= document length.
Average length and k1 are positive finite values <= 2**53; b is in [0,1].
Empty queries and zero-length documents score zero. Unseen terms may have
df zero. Rejects nonfinite intermediates/results; inputs are unchanged.

Caller supplies distinct-term alignment, corpus statistics and fitting
populations. No tokenization, text normalization, fitting, labels, query
weighting or task-specific policy. Positive IDF, exact lengths and (k1+1)
scale are explicit; no bitwise Lucene-equivalence claim.

limitations: Automated Tier 3 only; no human Tier 1 review or Tier 2 designation.
Validity bounds are caller contracts, not a claim that every invalid input or fabricated state is rejected.
Float64 numeric use is qualified; optional automatic monotonic direction has its stated statistical limitations.

Concrete runtime evidence does not prove existing text/isotonic witnesses value-preserving; abstract execution is not qualified.
115 prior tests, 12 native graph executions and eight semantic cases are source-bound current-platform evidence.
Semantic metadata must replace draft placeholder constraints; fit must record its exact isotonic dependency before activation.
Legacy metadata/state differs from new canonical drafts and must be handled explicitly during publication; no identity replacement.
